title: Relative coherent duality and trace for perfect images between nodal families
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $p:Y\to S$ and $q:Z\to S$ be proper, flat morphisms of finite presentation [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric fibres pure of dimension one [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. No marking, genus or contraction condition is imposed. Let $c:Y\to Z$ be a proper $S$-morphism. Use the canonical relative dualizing lines $\omega_{Y/S},\omega_{Z/S}$ with the adjunction normalization [def-trf-nodal-dualizing-datum]. Let $F$ be a perfect complex on $Y$, and suppose $Rc_*F$ is perfect on $Z$ [def-pc-perfect-complex]. There is a canonical trace-duality isomorphism in the derived category of quasi-coherent modules [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image]
$$Rc_*R\mathcal Hom_Y(F,\omega_{Y/S}[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_Z(Rc_*F,\omega_{Z/S}[1]).$$
Here $R\mathcal Hom$ is derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and $[1]$ denotes the cohomological shift of complexes. The map is induced by evaluation followed by the relative trace $Rc_*\omega_{Y/S}[1]\to\omega_{Z/S}[1]$, where that trace is the counit under the canonical identification $c^!\omega_{Z/S}[1]\simeq\omega_{Y/S}[1]$ and $c^!$ denotes the right adjoint to $Rc_*$. On any open of $Z$ over which $c$ is an isomorphism this is the usual identification, using the adjunction normalization of the dualizing lines. The isomorphism is natural in $F$ and in isomorphisms of the diagram. It commutes with every base change $S_{new}\to S$ under canonical derived base-change maps and the canonical base-change identifications of the relative dualizing complexes; for the new diagram take $F_{new}=Lg_Y^*F$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. These compatibilities respect composition of base changes.

source.place: Tags 0A9Q (lemma-iso-on-RSheafHom) and 0GEV (remark-iso-on-RSheafHom), perfect source and perfect direct image; relative form with traces from spaces-duality.tex Tags 0E5X (definition-relative-dualizing-proper-flat) and 0E6C (lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing); nodal identification moduli-curves.tex Tag 0E6R (lemma-gorenstein-dualizing). Agent formulation combining these statements, with proper Y/S and Z/S, not a claim that c is flat.

proof.text: Put $K_Y=\omega_{Y/S}[1]$ and $K_Z=\omega_{Z/S}[1]$. Apply [lem-sfb-gorenstein-curve-relative-dualizing] to $p,q$: their dualizing complexes are these invertible lines shifted by one, hence perfect and locally bounded. The completed rings in the nodal hypothesis can be taken as completed algebras by [lem-trf-rational-nodal-completion-algebra], on finite-type affine neighbourhoods in each geometric fibre. Therefore [lem-sfb-proper-nodal-dualizing-base-change] identifies these with the specified adjunction-normalized lines, including their canonical base-change identifications. The relative traces $\tau_p:Rp_*K_Y\to\mathcal O_S$ and $\tau_q:Rq_*K_Z\to\mathcal O_S$ are those of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality]; on affine bases they are precisely the coherent-adjunction counits under the Zariski-etale comparison stated there.

source.place: Tags 0E5X, 0E6C, 0E6E in spaces-duality.tex and 0E6R in moduli-curves.tex: adjunction normalization and arbitrary-base trace pairs.

proof.text: The new locality theorem [lem-sfb-proper-flat-families-coherent-adjoint-locality] supplies $c^!$, and also $p^!,q^!$ by using the flat identity family $S\to S$. The hypotheses are properness of these maps and flat local finite presentation of their source and target over $S$; no flatness of $c$ is used. Apply locality to $p^!\mathcal O_S,q^!\mathcal O_S$: on affine opens of $S$ these are the normalized trace pairs from step 1. Uniqueness of the relative dualizing trace pair therefore identifies them globally with $K_Y,K_Z$, including counits. Derived pushforward composition [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] identifies $Rp_*$ with $Rq_*Rc_*$. Right-adjoint composition [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] then gives the canonical identification $i:K_Y=p^!\mathcal O_S\xrightarrow{\sim}c^!q^!\mathcal O_S=c^!K_Z$. Define $t:Rc_*K_Y\to K_Z$ as $\varepsilon_c\circ Rc_*i$. The pasted-counit clause says exactly $\tau_q\circ Rq_*t=\tau_p$, with the direct-image composition comparison understood. Thus the trace is fixed by adjunction, rather than by an identification of line bundles alone.

source.place: Composition of adjunctions, normalized relative dualizing pairs, and Tag 0A9P locality.

proof.text:
Write $D=R\mathcal Hom_Y(F,K_Y)$ and $H=Rc_*F$. Both $D$ and $R\mathcal Hom_Z(H,K_Z)$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-sc-rhom-supported-qcoherent-perfect-part], using respectively the two separate hypotheses that $F$ and $H$ are perfect. Properness makes $c$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh] puts $Rc_*D$ in the same category. Use the concrete counit-defined pairing $q_c$ of [def-sc-mixed-direct-image-tensor-pairing]. Under [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-adjunction], define $d:Rc_*D\to R\mathcal Hom_Z(H,K_Z)$ as the transpose of
$$Rc_*D\otimes^LH\xrightarrow{q_c}Rc_*(D\otimes^LF)\xrightarrow{Rc_*\mathrm{ev}}Rc_*K_Y\xrightarrow{t}K_Z.$$
This specifies the actual evaluation-and-trace map in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0A9Q: evaluation/projection followed by the sheafy trace; Tag 0GEV: perfect coefficient and perfect image.

proof.text: Check invertibility over an affine open $W\subset S$. The schemes $Y_W,Z_W$ are qcqs, since they are proper over the affine scheme $W$; the restricted $c_W$ is proper and hence qcqs. The locality theorem identifies the restriction of $c^!K_Z$ and its counit with $c_W^!(K_Z|_{Z_W})$. Derived direct image restricts by [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open], and internal Hom restricts by the evaluation comparison of [lem-pc-open-restriction-evaluation-mate-is-iso]. Thus $d|_{Z_W}$ is the sheafy counit comparison of [lem-pc-qcqs-sheaf-rhom-adjunction] with $L=F|_{Y_W}$ and $K=K_Z|_{Z_W}$; its coherator is invertible. Both its endpoints are quasi-coherent by step 3. The inclusion in [lem-pc-dq-coherator-adjunction] is a full subcategory, so the counit $DQ(E)\to E$ is invertible for such endpoints, by the adjunction bijection and Yoneda. Hence $d|_{Z_W}$ itself is invertible. These opens cover $Z$: every cohomology sheaf of the cone vanishes on the cover and therefore vanishes. This proves $d$ invertible globally without assuming $S$ qcqs.

source.place: Tags 0A9Q and 0GEV; localization to affine opens of S, then erase the coherator on its full image.

proof.text: All arrows in step 3 are functorial, so transposing evaluation proves naturality in $F$ (contravariantly, as required for the dual). For an isomorphism of the diagram, transport each adjunction and its counit by that isomorphism. The unique counit-preserving comparisons of [lem-sfb-coherent-right-adjoint-comparisons] identify the resulting $i,t$ with those in step 2 and respect composition. Evaluation and the natural tensor-Hom bijection then identify $d$. On an open $V\subset Z$ where $c$ is an isomorphism, use the locality theorem at the locally bounded-below $K_Z$, and restriction of pushforward and internal Hom as in step 4. The adjunction for the equivalence $c_V$ identifies $c_V^!$ with its inverse and its counit with evaluation of that inverse. The counit equation for $i$ therefore makes $t|_V$ the usual identification; the transpose in step 3 is the usual internal-Hom identification. This also covers the identity map and empty opens.

source.place: Naturality of the adjunction comparison in Tag 0A9Q; canonical adjunction comparisons and restriction.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $a:S'\to S$, and use primes for its base changes and $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:Z'\to Z$. By [lem-sfb-flat-families-tor-independent] the square for $c$ is Tor independent, since $Y$ and $Z$ are flat over $S$. It follows that the canonical $\beta_E:Lv^*Rc_*E\to Rc'_*Lu^*E$ is invertible for every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$: restrict to affine opens in $Z$ and then affine opens in their inverse images in $Z'$, apply [lem-pc-tor-independent-perfect-tensor-base-change] with $P=\mathcal O$ and $K=E$, and use [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open]. The restriction identifies the canonical maps because their defining adjunction units restrict to the same units; the pasting identity [lem-pc-derived-base-change-horizontal-pasting] gives the same identification for the two successive open restrictions. Invertibility can be checked on this open cover. The same argument applies to $p,q$ using the flat identity family $S\to S$. In particular $H'=Rc'_*F'\simeq Lv^*H$. Since derived pullback preserves perfect complexes [lem-pc-derived-pullback-perfect], both $F'=Lu^*F$ and $H'$ are perfect, so the new diagram satisfies the coefficient hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 08IB, localized via the common-base Tor-independence criterion; never apply a flat-morphism theorem to c.

proof.text:
For clarity specify the right-adjoint base-change arrow globally as the transpose of
$$Rc'_*Lu^*c^!K\xrightarrow{\beta_{c^!K}^{-1}}Lv^*Rc_*c^!K\xrightarrow{Lv^*\varepsilon_{c,K}}Lv^*K.$$
The mate bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] makes this an unambiguous map $\alpha_c(K):Lu^*c^!K\to c'^!Lv^*K$. On qcqs charts it is precisely [def-sc-duality-equation-base-change-map], and its defining counit equation is
$$\varepsilon_{c',Lv^*K}\circ Rc'_*(\alpha_c(K))\circ\beta_{c^!K}=Lv^*\varepsilon_{c,K}.$$
Identify $Y'=Y\times_SS'$ with $Y\times_ZZ'$, so that the square for $p$ is the square for $c$ stacked on the square for $q$. By [lem-sfb-derived-base-change-vertical-pasting], under the composition identifications $Rp_*\simeq Rq_*Rc_*$ and $Rp'_*\simeq Rq'_*Rc'_*$ the base-change map $\beta_p$ is the paste $Rq'_*(\beta_c)\circ\beta_{q,Rc_*}$; hence $\beta_p^{-1}$ is the paste of the inverse squares $\beta_c^{-1}$ and $\beta_q^{-1}$. The generic mate-pasting identity [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (part 2), applied to these inverse base-change squares for $Rc_*$ and $Rq_*$ and the pasted composite adjunction, therefore says that $\alpha_p(\mathcal O_S)$ is the composite of $\alpha_c(K_Z)$ with $c'^!\alpha_q(\mathcal O_S)$ under the comparison $i$. This is a global adjunction calculation; no gluing of equality of arbitrary derived morphisms is being assumed.

source.place: Equation-base-change-map; Tag 0ATQ and generic pasting of adjunction mates. Explicit counit equation for the second mate. Vertical composition of base-change maps: cohomology.tex Tag 0ATL (remark-compose-base-change).

proof.text:
For $p$ and $q$, [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality] identifies the canonical pullback of the dualizing trace pair with the new trace pair for every $S'\to S$, including the structural counit. Thus its complex comparison is the transpose defining $\alpha_p(\mathcal O_S)$ and $\alpha_q(\mathcal O_S)$ in step 7; this follows directly from that transpose bijection and the trace-preserving equation. On qcqs bases its invertibility also follows from [lem-sc-proper-flat-right-adjoint-basechange], applied only to $p,q$, which are flat and finitely presented. Write these canonical identifications as $k_Y:Lu^*K_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{Y'}$ and $k_Z:Lv^*K_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{Z'}$; they are the line-bundle identifications of step 1. Pasting in step 7 now gives
$$c'^!(k_Z)\circ\alpha_c(K_Z)\circ Lu^*i=i'\circ k_Y.$$
Substitute this into the counit equation, then use naturality of $\varepsilon_{c'}$ and of $\beta$. The result is the trace square
$$t'\circ Rc'_*(k_Y)\circ\beta_{K_Y}=k_Z\circ Lv^*t.$$
In particular this proves the required trace compatibility even when $c$ is not flat.

source.place: Tags 0E6C, 0E6E and 0B6J: relative trace pairs and the trace/counit base-change square; no flatness assertion for c.

proof.text:
Put $D'=R\mathcal Hom_{Y'}(F',K_{Y'})$. The evaluation-mate comparison [lem-sc-mixed-perfect-internal-hom-pullback-isIso], followed by $k_Y$, gives $h_Y:Lu^*D\xrightarrow{\sim}D'$, since $F$ is perfect. The same theorem for the perfect $H$ gives $h_Z:Lv^*R\mathcal Hom_Z(H,K_Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{Z'}(Lv^*H,K_{Z'})$. Define
$$A=Rc'_*(h_Y)\circ\beta_D,\qquad B=R\mathcal Hom_{Z'}(\beta_F^{-1},1)\circ h_Z.$$
Their targets are $Rc'_*D'$ and $R\mathcal Hom_{Z'}(H',K_{Z'})$, respectively. In particular both canonical endpoint comparisons are isomorphisms, and the required base-change assertion has the precise form $d'\circ A=B\circ Lv^*d$.

source.place: Tag 0A6H: perfect internal Hom pullback is the invertible evaluation mate; comparison maps with their variance made explicit.

proof.text: Prove the last equation by applying the tensor-Hom bijection of [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-adjunction], and identify $H'$ with $Lv^*H$ by $\beta_F$. The definition of $h_Y$ identifies evaluation for $D',F'$ with the pullback of evaluation for $D,F$, followed by $k_Y$. Apply [lem-sc-mixed-tensor-pairing-base-change] with $f=c$, $g=v$, $A=D$, $B=F$, $C=K_Y$ and $a=\mathrm{ev}:D\otimes^LF\to K_Y$. Its displayed equation identifies the base change of $q_c;Rc_*\mathrm{ev}$ with $(\beta_D\otimes\beta_F);q_{c'};Rc'_*\mathrm{ev}'$, including the pullback tensorators. Composing with the trace square of step 8 identifies the two resulting pairings into $K_{Z'}$. The bijection is injective, so their transposes agree. This proves $d' A=B Lv^*d$ with the canonical maps of step 9, rather than only some isomorphism of the two complexes.

source.place: Tag 0B6J combined with the counit-defined tensor-pairing base-change identity; equality after taking evaluation transposes.

proof.text: For successive $S''\to S'\to S$, ordinary $\beta$ satisfies the explicit pasting equation [lem-pc-derived-base-change-horizontal-pasting]. The canonical mate bijection and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] therefore give the same pasting equation for $\alpha$; on qcqs charts this is also [lem-sc-right-adjoint-mate-successive-base-change]. The dualizing-pair comparisons $k_Y,k_Z$ satisfy composition and identity by [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality]. For the internal-Hom comparisons $h_Y,h_Z$, transpose their composite: by their defining evaluation formula its transpose is evaluation pulled back twice, followed by the composite $k$. Associativity and the identity comparison of derived pullback [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] identify this with the single composite-base-change transpose, so injectivity of the tensor-Hom bijection identifies the maps. Consequently the two composites of $A$ and $B$ in step 9 equal the comparisons for $S''\to S$, and the equation in step 10 respects composition and identity. All constructions also respect isomorphisms of diagrams by step 5.

source.place: Tags 0ATR, 0ATQ and 0E6C; canonical pasting, pullback associativity and uniqueness of evaluation transposes.
